To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the late-time entropy produced from the non-relativistic decay of massive particles can be a significant effect in the early universe, and the thermalization of neutrinos after this entropy production is properly treated by solving the Boltzmann equations for neutrino distributions.

the late-time entropy produced by decays of massive particles could be large enough to make a large fraction of the relic neutrinos not to be thermalized and the tight constraint on T_R from the BBN is relaxed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cosmological constraints on the late-time entropy produced by massive particles.
the late-time entropy productions due to the decay processes of non-relativisitic massive particles, such as gravitinos, axions and moduli fields.
the late-time entropy produced by massive particle decay and its effects on the big bang nucleo-synthesis, large scale structure formation, and cosmic microwave background.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the large entropy production is still allowed, but the constraints on the reheating and the entropy production are much looser than those in the standard picture.
the late-time entropy productions can be accommodated in the standard cosmological models without serious conflicts with observations.
the late-time entropy productions are not necessarily in contradiction with the standard big bang cosmology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a large entropy production does not have a significant effect on the cosmological evolution.
the large entropy production at late time t $\simeq$1 sec is not so strongly constrained by the present data.
a large entropy production at late-time t $\gtrsim$ 1 sec is not excluded by cosmological observations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
late time entropy production is a very interesting possibility for the dark matter candidate, which could be a good alternative to the WIMP paradigm.
the late-time entropy produced by the decay of nonrelativistic massive particles can significantly affect the evolution of neutrino temperature, and hence the thermalization of neutrinos.
the late time entropy production is a very efficient way to suppress the tight constraint on T_R from the nucleosynthesis.
